title: One local pivot for a free integral matrix with locally free rational cokernel
statement: Let ℓ be prime and E a normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra which is a field. Put O_E and its continuous coefficient sheaf R_X as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Let X be any scheme, A and B finite free R_X-modules, with A of rank n, and a:A→B. Suppose the cokernel of a after extension to the continuous E coefficient sheaf is pro-etale locally finite free. Then there is a pro-etale cover V→X such that, after the canonical coefficient pullback comparison, a is either zero or admits bases A|V≅R_V⊕A₁ and B|V≅R_V⊕B₁ with A₁ finite free of rank m<n and B₁ finite free, and block matrix ((p,r p),(c,d)), where p:R_V→R_V is monic and becomes invertible after extension of scalars to E. The maps r:A₁→R_V, c:R_V→B₁ and d:A₁→B₁ are integral module maps. No noetherianity or finite-dimensionality is assumed after the rational cokernel cover is supplied.

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: Refine the given rational finite-free cokernel cover. Use the continuous-function coefficient comparison and its compatibility with pullback to express the chosen finite free matrix as continuous O_E-valued functions, naturally under restriction.

On a piece where the rational cokernel has rank q and the target rank t, exact evaluation at an algebraically closed residue field identifies its fibre with the cokernel of the evaluated continuous matrix. Hence the pointwise E-rank is t-q throughout the piece. If the matrix vanishes at one point, this rank is zero and every continuous entry is zero everywhere on the piece. This supplies the zero alternative, including zero source or target ranks.

At every point of a nonzero rank piece choose an entry of maximal norm. On the finite intersection of the opens where the changes of all entries have norm strictly smaller than that pivot norm, the pivot is nowhere zero with constant norm and dominates all entries, by the ultrametric inequality. The first-row entries divided by the pivot are continuous E-valued functions with norm at most one, hence actual integral coefficient sections.

Permute the pivot column and row first and split off the corresponding regular summands. The remaining source rank is n-1<n. Assemble the first-row quotients into r and the remaining blocks into c and d; equality of continuous functions gives the displayed block identity. Pointwise cancellation on every site object proves that the pivot endomorphism is monic. After extension to E, multiplication by its continuous reciprocal is its inverse. Compose these open coverings with the supplied pro-etale covering. The empty scheme uses the empty cover.

proof_origin.place: One nonzero pivot in the continuous matrix argument
proof_origin.note: H2: strictly one pivot, without any kernel or finite-presentation conclusion. The parent proves strong induction and all cokernel, scalar-extension and stratification glue. Remaining formal work is coefficient matrix realization, exact fibre evaluation and its rank consequence, and assembly of the scalar pivot into the finite free bases. Edge cases checked: empty X, either zero rank, zero matrix, nonzero rank, and failure without the rational cokernel hypothesis. Blueprint ancestry follows the explicit target pointer to thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension because the ancestor helper cannot follow the existing module-valued created.item.

theorem integralMatrix_pivot_cover (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (E : Type) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E] :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Scheme.{u})
    (A B : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X)) (a : A ⟶ B),
    Nonempty (A ≅ Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) n) →
    Mod.IsFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) B →
    (∃ V : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X, ∀ k,
      Mod.IsFree ((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (V.f k)).obj
          (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X))
        (((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (V.f k)).mapMod _).obj
          ((Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).obj
            (cokernel a)))) →
    ∃ V : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X, ∀ k,
      let R := condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) (V.X k)
      let T := (ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (V.f k)).mapMod
          (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) ⋙
        Mod.comap (inv (condensedPullbackHom (integralCoeff ℓ E) (V.f k)))
      T.map a = 0 ∨
        ∃ (m : ℕ), m < n ∧
          ∃ (A₁ B₁ : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology (V.X k)) Ab.{u + 1}) R)
            (_ : A₁ ≅ Mod.finiteFree R m),
            Mod.IsFree R B₁ ∧
              ∃ (p : Mod.regular R ⟶ Mod.regular R), Mono p ∧
                IsIso ((Mod.extendScalars
                  (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) (V.X k))).map p) ∧
                ∃ (r : A₁ ⟶ Mod.regular R) (c : Mod.regular R ⟶ B₁) (d : A₁ ⟶ B₁)
                  (eA : T.obj A ≅ Mod.regular R ⊞ A₁)
                  (eB : T.obj B ≅ Mod.regular R ⊞ B₁),
                  eA.inv ≫ T.map a ≫ eB.hom =
                    biprod.lift (biprod.desc p (r ≫ p)) (biprod.desc c d)
